intro.en: Talk about getting along, relationships and shared actions with reciprocal pronouns.

salir con.en: to go out with; to date

nota.en: Here it refers to dating; it can also mean going out socially with someone.
In this lesson, it refers to ending a romantic relationship.

ligar.en: to flirt; to chat someone up

nota.en: Colloquial; the precise sense varies with context and region.
It means “argue” in a quarrel; it can also mean “discuss” a subject or issue.
Grammatically feminine even when it refers to a male partner; it can mean one partner or a couple.
Living with someone does not necessarily mean being a romantic couple.
Colloquial; it can mean a friend or a work colleague, depending on context and region.

conocerse.en: to meet, to get to know each other

casarse con.en: to marry; to get married to

texto.en:
With a plural subject, **nos**, **os** or **se** can show that people act on one another: **Nos conocimos** en la universidad; **Se abrazaron**. A reflexive action is different: **Ana y Luis se vistieron** means that each got dressed. Context helps distinguish the two readings.

**Nos** goes with **nosotros/as**; **os** goes with familiar **vosotros/as**, used in much of Spain; **se** can go with **ellos/as** or **ustedes**. In most of Latin America, speakers use **ustedes** with **se** and a plural verb: **Ustedes se conocieron**.

**Relationship vocabulary.** These expressions describe different experiences, not a fixed sequence or expected milestones: **conocerse**, **ligar**, **salir con** alguien, **enamorarse de** alguien, **convivir** or **vivir juntos**, **casarse con**, **discutir**, **romper con**, **hacer las paces**. Relationships differ; not everyone does all of these.

**Llevar + time expression + gerund** describes how long an ongoing activity has lasted: **Llevan cinco años saliendo**; **llevamos dos años viviendo juntos**. **Echar de menos** means to miss someone or something: **te echo de menos**.

In a quarrel, **discutir** means to argue; it can also mean to discuss a topic or issue.

frases.en: How did you and Ana meet?

frases.es: En una fiesta. Al principio nos llevábamos fatal.
frases.en: At a party. At first we got on terribly.
Really? But you have been dating for five years.

frases.es: Ya. Discutimos mucho, pero siempre hacemos las paces.
frases.en: Yeah. We argue a lot, but we always make up.
And aren't you planning to live together?

frases.es: Sí, en verano. Cuando Ana está de viaje, la echo mucho de menos.
frases.en: Yes, in the summer. When Ana is away, I miss her a lot.

Se.en: Se can go with ellos/ellas or ustedes; the subject here is nosotros.

pregunta.en: Complete: she broke up with her boyfriend.

**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about your relationships: who you get on with, who you argue with and how you make up.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud how you met an important person in your life and how the relationship has changed.
